messages:
omar: Heads-up from a prod repro: our sampleapp retried a request after a transient 5xx and the retried request authenticated as the OLD project-scoped key even though we rotated to an org key during the retry window. caused a permissions mismatch and a noisy alert.
leah: that sounds like the retry code captured the auth header at request start and replayed it, rather than asking the credential provider for a fresh token. which SDK/runtime?
omar: js-sdk v1.8.2 used in sampleapp. rust-sdk behaves differently (it re-reads creds on retry). interesting parity bug.
hiro: oh no. two problems then: (1) credential precedence/conflict (env vs cached file vs default REDWOOD_API_KEY naming), and (2) retry behavior should not reuse a stale header if credentials changed mid-flight.
sam: can you share repro steps/snippet?
omar: minimal repro: start with REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT set, issue request that triggers a 5xx, rotate env to REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG between attempts, confirm retry happens within client and observe outgoing principal. pseudo:```js
process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT = 'proj-old'
client.request(...)
// during retry window ops injects
process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY_ORG = 'org-new'
```
Observed: retried request sent with proj-old.
leah: thanks. That matches an implementation detail: js-sdk's http client captures headers earlier to avoid recomputing on every chunk. We should change it to call the credential provider at retry-time. Backcompat caveat: some users expect sticky identity for multi-chunk streams, but rotation semantics are reasonable to prioritize.
hiro: UX decision: do we document that credentials are immutable for the life of a request in current stable, and then change in next minor with clear migration? or fix now with a one-line warning that retries may use stale creds?
sam: propose: 1) quick patch in js-sdk: on retry, refresh auth header from credential provider (non-breaking), 2) add unit + e2e in sampleapp CI that covers mid-flight rotation, 3) update onboarding docs about env var names and precedence (recommend single REDWOOD_API_KEY or explicit REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT/ORG usage).
omar: also found surprising env names in customers: some set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT simultaneously. SDK parity should define exact precedence order: explicit scoped vars > single generic var > cached file > interactive. We should publish that in auth docs.
leah: agree. Also add a low-overhead warning when we detect different principals across retries in logs: `WARN: credential changed during request retry — new principal xyz used`. That would make debugging easier.
hiro: one more edge: long-lived streams that auto-reconnect should re-resolve creds per connection attempt. We need tests for stream reconnect too.
sam: assigning: @leah for JS retry PR (small change + unit tests), @hiro to add stream e2e and docs updates, @omar to add sampleapp CI test. I'll open an eng-runtime ticket to audit other SDKs for parity.
devex-bot: Created ticket DEVEX-7010: "SDK retry must refresh credential provider when replaying requests; unify cred precedence across SDKs". Linked repos: redwood/js-sdk, redwood/rust-sdk, sampleapp.
eng-runtime: noted. We'll run a quick audit and flag any runtime-level constraints (e.g., token caching TTLs, network cost).
omar: thanks all — this saved at least one pager. i'll drop repro logs into the ticket and add a tiny harness for CI. :thumbsup:
